question: The Iran stone inscription states that Samudragupta was chosen as king by his father because of his _____________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Devotion, pious conduct, and heroism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Iran stone inscription** is a historical record that describes the accomplishments and characteristics of **Samudragupta**, one of the greatest rulers of the **Gupta Empire**.
 
• This inscription highlights that **Samudragupta was chosen as the king by his father, Chandragupta I**, not based on wealth, age, or support from other kings, but due to his **devotion, pious conduct, and heroism**.
 
• These qualities were considered essential for a ruler in ancient India, as they symbolized strength, moral character, and dedication to duty. *Hence, the correct answer is "Devotion, pious conduct, and heroism."*
 
• The **Gupta period** is known as the **Golden Age of India**, and rulers like Samudragupta contributed significantly to this era's advancements in **art, culture, and governance**.
 
• The inscription also portrays Samudragupta as a capable and just ruler who upheld **Dharma** (righteousness) and was revered for his **military prowess** and **administrative skills**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Samudragupta:**

 
 
• Samudragupta (reigned circa **335–380 CE**) was the son of **Chandragupta I** and is often referred to as the **Napoleon of India** due to his military conquests.
 
• He expanded the Gupta Empire significantly through numerous campaigns and is credited with bringing much of **northern and central India** under Gupta rule.
 
• Apart from being a military genius, Samudragupta was also a great patron of **art and culture**, as evident from his support for music and poetry.
 
 
 
• **The Gupta Empire:**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire (circa 320–550 CE) is often referred to as the **Golden Age of India**, characterized by significant progress in **science, mathematics, astronomy, art, and literature**.
 
• It was during this period that **Aryabhata**, a prominent mathematician and astronomer, made groundbreaking contributions.
 
 
 
• **Iran Stone Inscription:**
 
 
• The inscription is a primary source of information about the **Gupta dynasty** and its rulers, providing insights into their **administration, conquests, and personal qualities**.
 
• It celebrates the virtues and military victories of Samudragupta, portraying him as an ideal king.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Samudragupta’s Rule:**

 
 
• Samudragupta is known for his **military campaigns**, which are described in the **Allahabad Pillar inscription**. He conquered several kingdoms in northern and southern India.
 
• He was a patron of **scholars, poets, and musicians**, and he himself was a skilled poet and musician, often depicted with a veena in his hands.
 
• His reign was marked by **political stability, economic prosperity, and cultural achievements**, making the Gupta period a hallmark of Indian civilization.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Samudragupta’s achievements laid the foundation for the Gupta Empire’s **dominance in the Indian subcontinent**, which continued under his successors like Chandragupta II.
 
• The Gupta rulers' administrative and military policies were instrumental in unifying diverse regions of India under a single political framework.
